rows.note: The OWL 2 EL saturation reasoner (a Whelk / whelk-rs derivative, no I/O, wasm-portable). Product path: ontomark-reason's classify facade drives `Saturation` (classify.rs:225), and ontomark-compile pulls it in through its default `whelk-el` feature. Its ⊥-left rule tests the superclass (reasoner.rs:493). The doc comment records that upstream tested the subclass (:484-487), and a named regression test pins the fix (entailments.rs:97). ONT-04 / XR-03 (2026-11-01-parallel-implementations.md:306) reports that the whelk-rs fork still carries the old rule. The fork is outside the pin set and was not read here. Only node text in OM-04 (04-emitters…md:123) names it; no topic cites a file inside it.

Build and gate tooling. CI runs `adr-ledger.sh check`, a sha256-pinned fetch of agentbox's ADR checker (ci.yml:35), and `test-plugin-consumer.sh` (ci.yml:62). The release workflow builds the plugin engine (release.yml:53), and the nightly evaluator runs `doc-strict.sh` (dream.config.json:46). `env.sh` is a developer convenience. No CI or nightly step runs `estate-guard.sh` (COV-E-F5). The comment in `build-plugin-engine.mjs` gives the wrong output location (COV-E-F9).

The ADR-OM-002 assessment reads its five exports at this pin. CI runs its node tests (ci.yml:12). It is consumed as a release tarball by ontomark-obsidian (package.json:25), whose graph view uses it (see src/views).
The workspace manifest: 13 members (Cargo.toml:3-17), dual licence (:23). The pipeline report cites `Cargo.toml:23` for D2.

Vitest units, the WASM harness and the e2e shim (`test/e2e`, staged and run with `--network none` by offline-test.mjs:40-49). The refresh audit at this pin executed and bounded these (the 69-check shim, :54).
Figure-generation tooling for the README's anatomy SVG. `kit/` and `scripts/` are copied from the anatomy skill under MIT (build.mjs:4). No package script or build step references it.

The plugin's UI surface: entity, query and graph panes, diff and ingest confirmation modals, and the result table. main.ts registers them (:13-18). Every DOM write goes through Obsidian's `createEl`/`setText` with `text:`; there is no innerHTML sink. Both modals resolve false on any close that is not Apply (diff-modal.ts:61-64; ingest-modal.ts:112-115), which matches the guarded-edit behaviour drawn in OM-09.4. The graph view mounts the shared `@dreamlab-ai/ontomark-graph` renderer (graph-view.ts:3,57). Its `openNote` has no error handling (COV-E-F8). `QueryView.run` re-runs classify on `not_classified` (query-view.ts:131-134) and has no stale-result guard.

Generated wasm-bindgen typings, `src/generated/web/ontomark_wasm.d.ts`, fetched with the pinned engine. Only this file is un-ignored (.gitignore:6), and build-wasm.mjs:40 fails if it changes without being committed.

Python podcast-transcript tooling: download, enrichment, and the `weekly_ingest.py` pipeline (Loom extraction to draft pages in `working/`). The live weekly and catch-up jobs run agentbox's Rust `podcast-ingest` binary (run-ingest.sh:11; run-catchup.sh:52). No agentbox script invokes the Python file, which is a superseded, divergent copy that an agentbox doc still names (COV-E-F3). Both copies call their output 'verified', but only a confidence threshold is applied (COV-E-F4). The other eight scripts are one-off batch downloaders and enrichers; none of them is scheduled.

Six vendored Obsidian community-plugin bundles. Four carry the esbuild banner 'THIS IS A GENERATED/BUNDLED FILE BY ESBUILD' (main.js:1-3). `daily-notes-editor` (Boninall) and `obsidian-outliner` (Viacheslav Slinko) have no banner, so their vendoring evidence is the third-party author in each `manifest.json`. The one non-vendored file, `.termux/setup.sh`, is a phone-side setup script that clones `jjohare/visionGraph-working` (:19-20). It is operator tooling with no product role.

The Narrative Gold Mine contact page, published with the site (`cp -r static/. site-data/`, publish.yml:262). It gift-wraps the message in the browser (NIP-17) and lazily imports the transport (contact.js:112). `nostr-contact.js` is the dreamlab-ai-website embed built at 08628f06 (:1). That is the latest commit touching `src/lib/nostr.ts` and `scripts/contact-embed/` at the website pin, so the bundle is current. It is byte-identical (sha256 2b6bd4b2…) to VisionFlow's `website/static/js/nostr-contact.js` at VisionFlow worktree HEAD b105a94, which is not a pin, and VF-02 describes that copy. `contact.js` differs from VisionFlow's copy only in its defaults (topic and source tag).

An Open WebUI ComfyUI adapter kept as a note attachment ('copy into open-webui container', Server Setup.md:246). It imports `config.SRC_LOG_LEVELS` (:9), and no `config.py` exists in the repository. Nothing imports it.
The ADR-0001, -0004 and -0007 assessments at b77093e read the 10-column ledger, `rowContract.ts` and the proposer. DE-M1 records the whitespace-contract divergence from Rust.

The GitHub Pages site (pages.yml:31). It contains a vendored three.js r168 (MIT header) and a decorative tesseract hero. The dashboard renders an illustrative `data/ledger.json` and says so ('Sample data… not the output of a real nightly run', dashboard.html:138-141). It is not product code; no defect found.

'Optional semantic memory' over past nights. Only the workspace build, CI tests and README reach it; no package in the repository imports it. The RuVector path is not implemented, and an explicit request returns the flat-file store labelled `ruvector-rvf` (COV-E-F1; self-improvement.md:79, dated 2026-09-04, notes this too). A corrupt store is silently reset and then overwritten (COV-E-F2).
Read at b77093e: paste-in `/schedule` routine body only (`packages/schedule/src/index.ts:4-6,112-118`).
Read at b77093e: the witness `sha256(sha256(report)+commit)` (`packages/witness/src/index.ts:49-53`), with a single-byte mutation test.

The operator CLI for the kit's two pinned sidestr chains: holdings, issue, send, and a kind-23501 faucet. It replays either header family. Product path: agentbox's faucet runner execs it for BLAKE2b-parent chains (run-faucet.sh:60). A ledger that cannot be parsed is a hard error (faucet.rs:75-79). The producer-refused-but-relay-accepted path is documented behaviour (faucet_run.rs:9-10). A failed ledger save is only logged (COV-E-F6). Crate version 1.0.0-beta.15, `publish = false`.

Agentic-QE (AQE) agent-harness helpers: a hook shim, the statusline, a brain checkpoint, an advisor-call helper and a quality-criteria HTML validator. Two of them say they were 'generated by aqe init' (brain-checkpoint.cjs:3, statusline-v3.cjs:3). No workspace member, build or CI step references `.claude/`.

Workspace-wide wasm32 link flag `--max-memory=268435456` (:1-2). It caps every wasm32 build, including the trunk-built forum client, at 256 MiB of linear memory. There is no default target, so native tests run (:4-6). A grep of `docs/diagrams` and `docs/estate-review` for `max-memory` or `268435456` finds no mention.

The single source for the figures the site states, and the workshop display map. Pages import them (Header, Index, Programmes, Team, Workshop*, og-meta). The test checks only the specialist count and retired figures in the static files; prices are not checked. '£8M+' is hand-typed in three pages, despite site-facts.ts:2 (COV-E-F7).

`useOGMeta` feeds both the browser meta update and the build-time prerender through `StaticMetaContext` (prerender.tsx:58), which DW-02's prerender panel relies on. `useIsMobileSync` resolves on the first render so phones never mount the desktop tree. Workshop progress is per-browser localStorage that fails soft (:16, :23). No defect found.

An offline build for the A4 print flyer (WeasyPrint to `public/downloads/`). The flyer's figures match site-facts at this pin (40+, £995, £2,500), but the build says it hand-writes them and no test checks them (build.mjs:14-16). See COV-E-F7.

`spa-redirect.js`: deep-link restore, kept external because of the CSP. DW-01.7 and DW-02 describe it in prose and node text but do not list it under `sources:`. Re-read at the pin: scheme 1 refuses protocol-relative paths (:16), and scheme 2 relies on `replaceState` same-origin enforcement.
The Vitest setup file (jest-dom matchers and a matchMedia stub), wired only as `setupFiles`.

findings.summary: The module header says nights are stored as vectors in an RVF container for HNSW recall when RuVector is installed. In fact `openMemory` always builds `FlatMemory`, and with `backend: 'ruvector-rvf'` it overwrites the label to `ruvector-rvf` (:169).
findings.consequence: A caller or telemetry that reads `backend` is told semantic recall is active while keyword scoring runs. Recall quality claims built on that label are false.

findings.summary: `load` turns any read or JSON parse failure into an empty list (:81-83). The next `remember` then persists that list over the file (:99-100 → :91).
findings.consequence: A store that is corrupt or partly written, for example after an interrupted non-atomic `writeFile` (:91), is silently wiped on the next write, and all prior nights are lost. No package in the repository calls it yet, so there is no product exposure today.

findings.summary: `visionGraph/transcripts/weekly_ingest.py` presents itself as the weekly cron job, but the live jobs run agentbox's Rust port. The two have diverged: Python keeps confidence ≥ 0.7 flat (:486), while Rust uses tier thresholds of 0.7, 0.5 and 0.4 (verify.rs:13-20). An agentbox reference doc still names the Python file as an implementation of `write_assertion_ledger`, and XR-12 cites its `split_frontmatter` (:117) as a parallel parser.
findings.consequence: A maintainer who edits or runs the Python copy changes nothing in production, or lands drafts under the older rules. Corpus references to it describe a path that does not run.

findings.summary: Both ingest paths name their output 'verified' (Python docstring: 'verifies them via Perplexity'). Phase 3 only filters by the model's self-reported confidence, and no external check runs in cron mode.
findings.consequence: Draft pages and ledger bullets carry LLM claims as 'verified' that nothing has checked. The drafts stay in `working/` and need governed promotion, so the effect is limited to mislabelled evidence. A grep of `docs/diagrams/agentbox` and `docs/diagrams/estate` for `phase_verify` finds nothing, and none of their `pass-through` hits concerns the podcast pipeline.

findings.summary: The legacy-toolchain migration guard is not run by CI, the release workflow or the nightly evaluator. It scans sibling checkouts on disk, and its `legacy-crate` condition (`project/crates/vault-core` present, :146-147) holds at the VisionClaw pin. The script was not run.
findings.consequence: The DEPRECATION/EXP-10 migration has no enforcing gate. Residue can grow without any signal, and the guard can only be run by hand against working trees.

findings.summary: After a grant is sent, a failed ledger save is only logged (:194-196), and the save neither fsyncs nor checks the rename beyond `?` (:70-74). The in-memory ledger keeps enforcing limits until the process restarts.
findings.consequence: A restart after a failed save forgets those grants, so the faucet can pay the same script again within its window. That defeats the stated rationale ('forgetting grants would pay everyone again', faucet.rs:75-76). The impact is bounded because these chains' coins carry no value (lib.rs:33).

findings.summary: site-facts claims to be the one place pages take figures from. Its guard test checks only the specialist count and retired figures, not prices or accommodation. '£8M+' is typed by hand in three places, and the print flyer's prices are hand-copied with no check.
findings.consequence: `index.html` and `public/llms.txt` state no prices, so they are not at risk. The print flyer hand-copies the prices. It matches at this pin, but a change to site-facts.ts would leave it stale with CI green. `content/site-content.yaml`, which the test reads, already disagrees with site-facts ('£2999 · One-day intensive', :54, against `priceSprintFrom` £2,500), and the test does not catch it. Only its testimonials are consumed (generate-testimonials.mjs:6), so this stale copy is not rendered today.

findings.summary: `openNote` awaits `api.index` without a try/catch, and both callers discard the promise with `void` (:57, :64).
findings.consequence: When the index fails (for example after an engine error), double-clicking or pressing 'Open note' gives no feedback and an unhandled rejection is raised. The other views report errors through `statusEl` or `reportError`.
